LESSON: WESTERN MUSICAL INSTRUMENTS (SOLO PERFORMER)

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Performing
Topic 2.4: Western Musical Instruments (Solo Performer)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Western Musical Instruments (Solo Performer), part of Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: Why do instruments sound differently while playing the same pitch? 2. How is proficiency developed in playing a Western solo instrument?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. observe pictures or real instruments and identify various parts and their role in the production of sound,

2. tune or explain the tuning of a selected Western solo instrument. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology (Apply this adaptation in the subsequent learning experiences involving manipulation),

3. prepare a rehearsal schedule for practicing 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. observe pictures or real instruments and identify various parts and their role in the production of sound,
2. tune or explain the tuning of a selected Western solo instrument. Learners with manipulation difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or use assistive technology (Apply this adaptation in the subsequent learning experiences involving manipulation),
3. prepare a rehearsal schedule for practicing 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Western Musical Instruments (Solo Performer) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Citizenship: The learner gains skills in playing a solo musical instrument from the rest of the world (western) gaining

international awareness.

• Digital Literacy: The learner downloads; watches and listens to professional musicians perform Western instruments.

• Self-Efficacy: The learner confidently executes playing techniques that are specific to the selected Western solo

instrument.

Values:
• Integrity: The learner uses the internet appropriately when searching for music pieces to play.

• Responsibility: The learner uses instruments and digital devices as learning resources with utmost care.

• Respect: The learner respects others’ views during rehearsal sessions of the western instrument.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Online safety: The learner responsibly sources for instrumental music to play from the internet.

• Life skills: The learner acquires music reading skills that will help in interpreting scored music.

Suggested Learning Resources

Exercise books, Sheet music, Portfolios, Anecdotal records, Song books, ICT devices, Internet connectivity,

Props and costumes, Resource persons, Traditional Western Musical instruments, Audio/visual recordings of Western

style solo instrument, Pitching devices and Textbooks
